editorial_fulfillment.actual_excerpt:
Build one reusable demo pack before contacting vendors. Give every seller the same inputs:

- A common service job with an urgent reschedule, a return visit, parts used, field photos, customer approval, and an invoice.
- A recurring maintenance job with asset history, a checklist, a failed inspection item, follow-up work, and customer communication.
- A project or longer job with labor, materials, purchasing, progress billing, change handling, and a profitability report if that work matters to the business.
- A roster of current users and expected hires, split by office, field, management, subcontractor, and limited-access roles.
- Technician devices for hands-on field testing, a sample import file, and a map of accounting or ERP connections.
- A worksheet for package components, onboarding work, ongoing services, and likely expansion.

editorial_fulfillment.actual_excerpt:
Use the buyer scorecard after pass-or-fail requirements remove obvious mismatches. Score the remaining tools across workflow fit, field usability, implementation effort, integration needs, reporting and control, pricing structure, and support. Define each condition before a demo, keep evidence beside every score, and carry unresolved issues into the next round instead of treating them as assumptions.

| Criterion | Evidence to collect | Pass signal |
|---|---|---|
| Workflow depth | One real job traced from intake through payment | Required handoffs work without duplicate entry |
| Integrations and data | System map, data owners, import and export test | Required records move with clear ownership |
| Implementation effort | Named owner, timeline, migration, training plan | Work and accountability fit available capacity |
| Field adoption | Technician test on actual devices and conditions | Core steps stay clear in the field |
| Reporting and control | Sample dashboards, exceptions, permissions | Each role gets actionable visibility |
| Pricing and total cost | Written quote, add-ons, services, renewal terms | Current and future costs are comparable |
| Support | Channels, hours, onboarding, escalation path | Support matches operational risk |
